name: Scheme
title: Scheme (R7RS)

type.text: **No static type check**: A binding has no declared type and a call is resolved when it runs, so a type error is reported at run time rather than at load time
**Dispatch is dynamic**: An application checks its argument count and its operands' types when it executes, so an over-application or an under-application is an error then

**No sum types and no generics in the core**: An alternative is a tagged list whose tag the code must test by hand, and a reusable procedure accepts any object and documents its expectation in a comment (T4, T5)
**`+` and the other arithmetic procedures are ordinary bindings**: A redefinition changes what `(+ a b)` means, so an expression can invoke code the syntax does not show
**Hygienic macros decouple a macro from its use site**: `syntax-rules` renames the identifiers a template introduces, so a macro cannot accidentally capture a name from the caller
**Lexical scope is one small rule**: A `lambda` binds its parameters and its internal definitions, and nothing else is visible

construction.text: **Constructors are ordinary procedures**: A record constructor or a `lambda` that returns a list is built with the same mechanism, so construction does not couple to a class system
**`define-record-type` declares the shape once**: The R7RS form generates the constructor, the type predicate, and the field accessors from one declaration
**Proper tail recursion is a language guarantee**: A tail call reuses the current frame, so a loop written as a tail-recursive procedure runs in constant stack space
**`let` confines a binding to its body**: A construction can build its state inside a `let` and expose only what it returns
**`set!` lets a construction mutate a captured binding**: A closure can change state that its caller still holds, so a value built by a procedure is not automatically immutable
**A plain program has one top-level environment**: R7RS `define-library` with explicit `export` confines a set of bindings, but a program's top-level `define`s share a single scope
**One value, many names**: pairs are shared, and set! mutates every name that reaches the cell

memory.text: **A garbage collector reclaims memory**: The implementation chooses the collector, and the program cannot free an object or predict when it dies

**No RAII or scope-exit destructor**: A resource is released by an explicit call, and `dynamic-wind` can wrap that call in a dynamic extent, but nothing runs automatically at the end of an arbitrary scope
**No ownership or borrow model**: A reference is an untracked alias, and the collector alone knows when an object is unreachable
**No manual deallocation**: There is no free operation in the language, so a program cannot release a live object by mistake
**`dynamic-wind` binds a release to the dynamic extent**: Its `after` thunk runs on every exit, including a non-local one
**R7RS pairs acquisition with release in the common cases**: `call-with-port`, `with-input-from-file`, and `with-output-to-file` close what they open
**The undeclared class has no catch**: recursion crashes the implementation below the handler surface (the implementation's stack is not a declared failure)

error.text: **A failure is raised and is not described by a signature**: A procedure promises nothing about the conditions it may raise, so the failure set is not readable from the call
**`guard` gives a structured handler**: An R7RS `guard` clause names a condition and a recovery expression, and the handler returns a value to the `guard`
**`with-exception-handler` installs a handler for a dynamic extent**: The handler is bound where it is installed, not at the raise point
**Condition types form a small hierarchy**: `error-object?`, `file-error?`, and `read-error?` distinguish a raise by kind
**`error` carries a message and irritants**: The offending values travel with the condition
**`raise` and `raise-continuable` differ**: A non-continuable raise does not return to the raise point, so a handler must transfer control explicitly
**A fault ends the program**: the standard leaves toplevel recovery to the implementation and declares no recoverable unit

concurrency.text: **The core defines no shared-memory concurrency**: R7RS specifies no threads, so the standard makes no promise about a race the language does not create
**Continuations separate control flow from the call stack**: `call/cc` captures the current continuation as a procedure, so a coroutine, a generator, or a backtracking search is a library over it
**Parallelism is an implementation extension**: SRFI-18 supplies threads and SRFI-21 supplies synchronisation, and an implementation may support neither
**A thread extension fixes no memory model**: SRFI-18 defines a mutex and a condition variable, but the report it extends states no ordering guarantee for a shared object
**A cooperative scheduler is expressible in the language**: A queue of continuations plus a trampoline gives green threads without a runtime thread

platform.text: **No single implementation owns the language**: The language is a published report, and Chez, Guile, Racket, CHICKEN, Gambit, MIT, and Chibi all implement it
**`define-library` is the portability unit**: An R7RS library with explicit `import` and `export` moves between implementations with its source
**The core is small enough for a small runtime**: The report's language fits a microcontroller interpreter and an embeddable one
**A program runs under several evaluation strategies**: A compiler such as Chez and a simple interpreter both accept the report's subset
**The standard is a family of reports, not one**: R5RS, R6RS, and R7RS are not fully compatible, so the name "Scheme" alone does not say which report a program targets
**The library set beyond R7RS-small is the implementation's**: Each dialect ships a different collection, so portability in practice follows the chosen implementation

performance.text: **Native compilers are available**: Chez Scheme, Gambit, and CHICKEN compile Scheme to native code, so a program need not be interpreted
**The core is small enough to compile well**: A compiler sees the whole language, so a straightforward optimiser covers it
**Tail calls do not consume stack**: A recursive loop compiles to a jump
**Numeric code is fast in the strong implementations**: A fixnum loop compiles to machine operations when the compiler proves the operands are fixnums
**Performance varies significantly by implementation**: The same program can be fast under Chez and much slower under a simple interpreter
**A dynamically typed call is a checked call**: The compiler inserts checks the program did not write, and their cost depends on how well it can eliminate them

ecosystem.text: **The ecosystem is small and spread over implementations**: R7RS-small ships no library set, and the shared material is the SRFI collection plus each implementation's own packages
**The SRFIs are a portable library standard**: A program requests a library by number, and an implementation reports the SRFIs it supports
**The implementation distributions are mature and maintained**: Guile, Chez, Racket, Gambit, and CHICKEN are long-lived projects with their own package collections
**`snow` and the implementation indexes collect R7RS libraries**: A portable library can be published for several implementations at once
**Package management is implementation-specific**: `raco pkg`, `chicken-install`, and Guix each serve one dialect, and the report fixes no package manager
**A library that uses a dialect extension is not portable**: A program written against one implementation's collection usually needs editing for another

evolution.text: **SRFIs extend the language without changing the report**: A new facility arrives as a numbered request, and each implementation adopts it independently
**A program written to R7RS-small keeps its meaning**: The small report is stable, so its subset does not move under the program
**`define-library` localises a change to its importers**: An exported name is the interface, and a change inside a library is invisible to the code that imports it
**Three reports are in circulation and they differ**: R5RS, R6RS, and R7RS disagree on libraries, on the details of `syntax-rules`, and on some standard procedures
**An improvement reaches a program when an implementation adopts it**: There is no single body that ships the language, so the timing is the implementation's decision

domain.text: **Excellent as a teaching language**: A dozen special forms cover the core, and SICP uses the language as a complete course
**Excellent for programming-language research**: A small core with hygienic macros and first-class continuations is a substrate for experiments
**A real scripting and extension language**: Guile is the extension language of GNU packages, including the Guix package manager
**Embedding is a real use**: A small Scheme interpreter is embedded in applications for configuration and scripting
**Commercial application work is rare**: Adoption is niche, so a team that picks Scheme for a product finds few precedents

learning.text: **The distinctive abstractions take real effort**: `call/cc`, continuation-passing style, and hygienic macro writing are each a skill that takes time
**The core is small enough to learn quickly**: The special forms are few, and a complete course in them exists
**A REPL returns the value immediately**: The read-eval-print loop gives feedback on each expression
**The report is precise about the language it defines**: The specification states the required behaviour of each procedure
**The report is a specification, not a tutorial**: A beginner needs a text such as SICP alongside it
**A continuation is easy to use outside its intended extent**: Control that re-enters a captured continuation can surprise the programmer

syntax.text: **The syntax is uniform**: A program is a sequence of S-expressions, so there is almost no grammar to learn
**Prefix notation removes precedence rules**: `(+ 1 (* 2 3))` states the order in brackets, so no operator-precedence table is needed
**Quasiquotation makes a template readable**: `` `(a ,b ,@c) `` builds a list with holes at the point of use
**The reader recognises the literal syntaxes directly**: `#\a` is a character, `#(1 2)` is a vector, and `#;` comments out the next datum
**A macro can add a readable form**: `define-syntax` with `syntax-rules` introduces surface syntax without changing the core
**A deeply nested expression needs the editor's indentation**: The reader balances the brackets, and the human eye follows the layout

testing.text: **SRFI-64 defines a portable test framework**: `test-begin`, `test-equal`, and `test-end` run under any implementation that supports the SRFI
**`error` makes a check cheap to write**: `(unless test (error "..." x))` fails a check and reports the offending value
**The REPL is the first test loop**: An expression is evaluated and its value is compared at the prompt
**The implementation supplies a tracer and a debugger**: Chez, Guile, and Racket each expose a trace facility and an inspector
**No test framework is in the standard**: A project depends on its implementation's SRFI coverage rather than on the report
**A test exercises the paths it runs**: An unexecuted branch is unchecked, and a dynamic error in it appears only when the branch is reached
**No monotonic reading published**: the standard's current-second is the wall; the program's durations have no published clock

security.text: **The implementation manages memory**: The language exposes no pointer and no manual free, so a buffer overflow or a use-after-free is not expressible in Scheme source
**Hygienic macros remove a class of capture defect**: A macro cannot bind a name it did not intend to bind
**The core has no unsafe memory operation**: The report defines no pointer arithmetic and no address
**`eval` and `read` execute data as code**: `(eval (read port))` runs whatever the input contains, so untrusted input must never reach it
**A continuation can cross an intended check**: A continuation captured before a permission test can be re-entered after it
**A foreign-function interface leaves the safe subset**: An FFI in an implementation reaches native code, and the memory-safety guarantee stops there

reproducibility.text: **No contract the implementation reads**: the R7RS import system names libraries, not versions, and no machine-read manifest ships

tradeoffs: **The minimalist core is a deliberate trade**: The report defines a small language and leaves libraries to the SRFIs, so a program chooses its extensions
**The report split is a standards history**: R5RS, R6RS, and R7RS followed a disagreement about how large the language should be
**Dynamic typing is a design choice**: No type declaration is required, so the discipline is the programmer's
**`call/cc` is a powerful and uncommon operator**: Full continuations make control flow harder to reason about, and the expressiveness is the return
**The REPL-first workflow is a choice**: A program is developed at the prompt, which suits exploration and is not required by the language
**Niche adoption is a scope outcome**: The language targets education and research rather than industry
verdict: Scheme's minimalist, orthogonal core keeps language-imposed coupling low, and its platform cost is moderate. Proper tail recursion removes stack growth from a recursive loop, hygienic macros prevent name capture, first-class continuations separate control flow from the call stack, and `define-library` confines a set of bindings behind explicit exports. The core score is held down by dynamic typing, absent sum types and generics, garbage-collected memory with no ownership model or RAII, and unchecked exceptions. Main weakness: the ecosystem is small and the standard is fragmented across R5RS, R6RS, and R7RS.

energy.text: Compiles to native code: the fastest class in the language energy and time benchmarks [@pereira2017energy; @pereira2021ranking]. A causal re-analysis attributes the difference to execution time [@vankempen2025green].

ai-readiness.text: Sparse training data: models write it unreliably [@joel2025lowresource].

safety.text: No certified or standards-qualified path for safety-critical systems.

delivery.note: Each implementation loads source and compiles it on the target
